plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Bare branches burst into fragrant blossoms in pink, white and deep rose. They open in the cold, often before the leaves appear, and fill Japanese plum groves and temple gardens with a spicy-sweet scent.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter, roughly January to March, peaking in February
plants.location: Japan, with the same bloom in China and Korea
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a traditional symbol of perseverance in East Asia because they flower through the last frosts of winter, weeks ahead of cherry blossoms.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, white bell-shaped flowers with green-tipped inner petals push up through cold soil, and sometimes through snow. Woodlands and gardens fill with drifts of them as winter ends.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, mainly February to March
plants.location: Temperate Europe and in gardens across the Northern Hemisphere, including the northern United States
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make a natural antifreeze-like protein that helps them survive freezing conditions. They also gave science galantamine, a compound used in medicine for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems carry round clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers in shades of blue, violet and white above strappy evergreen leaves. They make a bold show in summer gardens and along coastal bush.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer in the Southern Hemisphere, about December to February and sometimes later
plants.location: Eastern Cape, South Africa, and summer gardens across the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, it is not a true lily. Its name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'.
